subject: Clarify public-facing language for data transfers, SCCs, and subprocessors
messages:
From: Sophia Blake <sophia.blake@acme.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Legal Team <legal@acme.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Public snippet request — data transfers / subprocessors

Hi Dylan / Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this on. Acme's privacy team is reviewing the language we'll include in our product UI and vendor inventory. Two asks: 1) a one-paragraph, consumer-facing sentence (<= 60 words) explaining how Redwood may transfer customer data outside the EEA and what safeguards apply (we'd prefer something we can paste into our Help Center); 2) a short, plain-language note explaining subprocessors and where to find the list.

From our side, legal wants explicit mention of the mechanism (SCCs) and a clear link to the subprocessor list; they also asked us to avoid legalese like "data processing transfers" if possible.

Can you share a draft snippet and indicate whether the Console copy can show the subprocessor list and last-updated date? Also please attach any high-level explainer (SCCs / alternatives) we can share internally.

Best,
Sophia
Sophia Blake
Senior Counsel, Privacy — Acme Corp

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Public snippet request — data transfers / subprocessors

Hi Sophia — thanks for the clear asks.

Quick plan: Kimberly and Laura will draft a consumer-friendly paragraph plus a short subprocessor note; I attached an initial two-line option to get us started (see attachment). We can iterate quickly — happy to hop on a 30-min call tomorrow if helpful.

We can show an always-updated subprocessor list in the Console with a "last updated" timestamp; I'll confirm retention and how often the list is refreshed.

Attached: draft-privacy-snippet.txt (very short initial wording).

Next steps: Kimberly, can you take the lead on the wording and also prepare a short explainer we can share with Acme's privacy team? Laura, LMK if you want to comment on the Console UX note.

Thanks,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachment: draft-privacy-snippet.txt (1)
From: Sophia Blake <sophia.blake@acme.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-21T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Public snippet request — data transfers / subprocessors

Dylan — thanks. A couple of quick clarifications from Acme Legal:

- Please avoid references to outdated frameworks (e.g., "Safe Harbor"). We need explicit mention of SCCs (standard contractual clauses) as the legal basis for cross-border transfers, and a short sentence explaining Acme customers can request data residency where offered.
- The Console subprocessor list is critical for our procurement team; can it be a CSV download with a last-updated timestamp?

If you can send a slightly longer explainer (two short paragraphs) that our ops folks can forward to procurement, that would be ideal.

Sophia

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sophia Blake <sophia.blake@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-22T11:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Public snippet request — data transfers / subprocessors

Hi Sophia — thanks for the guidance. Below is a proposed set of customer-facing copy and a short explainer for procurement. We kept wording plain and avoided legal jargon where possible. Happy to tweak.

Consumer-facing UI snippet (one paragraph, ~45 words):
"Redwood may transfer customer data to countries outside the European Economic Area when necessary to provide our services. We protect transfers using the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) and additional safeguards (encryption, access controls). For data residency options, see Console settings or contact support."

Subprocessor note (short):
"We use third‑party subprocessors to operate and improve the service (hosting, monitoring, analytics). Our Console lists current subprocessors and includes a 'last updated' date — you can download the list as CSV."

Procurement-facing explainer (two short paragraphs):
"1) Transfer mechanism: Redwood relies on the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) for cross-border transfers and implements technical and organizational safeguards — including customer-managed KMS options, point-in-time logging, and limited access controls — to reduce risk.

2) Subprocessors and transparency: We publish a current subprocessor list in the Console (CSV download) and notify customers ahead of material changes. For regulated customers we offer Private deployment and contractual commitments to restrict subprocessors or enable on-premises hosting."

Attachments: SCC explainer (PDF) and latest subprocessor list (CSV).

Laura: for the Console copy, I recommend we add a small "Learn more" link that opens the SCC explainer and the CSV download. Marcus — can you confirm we can show the CSV download and timestamp in the current Console build and estimate an ETA?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Privacy Counsel — Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: scc-explainer.pdf, subprocessor-list.csv
